newsitem.title: UK: Gold drops to 3-1/4 year nadir as speculators sell.
newsitem.headline: Gold drops to 3-1/4 year nadir as speculators sell.

text.p: Gold prices slid further on Monday afternoon, hitting fresh three-year lows as the metal came under a fresh onslaught from speculators.
"Everything is still pointing south. Gold doesn't have a lot going for it," one London dealer said.
Gold, which fixed at $358.50 per ounce on Monday afternoon, has shed about $10 in the first few days of the New Year.
The metal was vulnerable to more steep losses over the next several weeks, but may take a breath of air and stabilise over the coming few days, analysts and dealers said.

Gold has been shunned by investors since it came off a blistering rally around this time last year that took it to $416. They have seen little reason to put money in gold, a traditional "safe haven", as U.S. inflation remains stable.
A galloping stock market has also siphoned attention and money away from precious metals. The Dow Jones Industrial average shot up 101.60 points to 6,544.09 on Friday.
"This is the first week of the new year and we're at three-year lows," said analyst Ted Arnold of Merrill Lynch.
"Increasingly it looks like the downside is wide open. In 1997, I think $330 looks possible."
Bullion fixed at $359.25 an ounce in the morning, the lowest since October 7, 1993 and down sharply from the Friday afternoon fixing of $364.00.
Investment funds, anticipating still lower prices, have sold the market heavily "short", and professional dealers have followed the trend.
Expected buying by jewellery manufacturers, mainly from the Far East, have failed to support the market. Many buyers are standing aside, waiting for lower prices, dealers said.
Fear that European central banks will sell some of their gold reserves to qualify for the entry to the European Monetary Union has also dulled gold's shine.
Some analysts noted that the market was due for greater price volatility this year, as a price "stranglehold" created by holders and grantors of options was broken.
Options give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.
"Once you break free of options, the fundamentals take over. The fundamentals are bearish, and the charts are turning bearish, so the funds are selling. It's a downward spiral," Arnold said.
Near term volatilities for over the counter, or off-exchange, gold options have shot up by 2.5 percentage points to 10 percent over the past few days, option dealers said.
Technical analysts agreed that historical price charts pointed to more losses for gold.
"Selling pressure has increased across this complex, forcing new lows," said technical analyst Elli Gifford, of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Some dealers put initial support for gold at a historical chart point around $358, while brokers Rudolf Wolff said there was little propping up values above $350 an ounce.
The other precious metals, particularly platinum, were also suffering from gold's weakness.
Platinum like gold fixed at a 3-1/4 year low of $361.75 an ounce on Monday afternoon down $4.25 from Friday's afternoon fixing.
Silver and palladium suffered less than the others, with silver indicated one cent below Friday's closing level at $4.67 an ounce and palladium $1.45 off at $118.75 an ounce.
